sentences.text: The genus name Zuolong honors General Zuo Zongtang, combining his name with the Chinese word for dragon. This general secured the region of Xinjiang for China.
The holotype specimen IVPP V15912 includes a partially complete skull and many post-cranial bones. The skull is triangular-shaped with a snout that tapers significantly towards the end.

Thomas R. Holtz Jr. considers the holotype specimen to almost certainly belong to a juvenile theropod. Gregory S. Paul hypothesized that the holotype is a juvenile and estimated an adult length of 3 meters and a mass of 50 kg.
Some authors suggest an adult Zuolong reached a length of 3.35 meters and a mass of 43 kg.
The fossil of Zuolong was discovered in the Shishugou Formation in Xinjiang, China. The holotype fossil was found in 2001 in the upper part of the formation near Wucaiwan.
The genus was described by Choiniere et al. in 2010. The description was published by Jonah Choiniere, James Clark, Catherine Forester, and Xu Xing. The type species is Zuolong salleei.
The most common hypothesis regarding Zuolong's taxonomy is that it is a basal member of Coelurosauria.
A 2022 phylogeny by Rolando and colleagues included Zuolong in their analysis. Andrea Cau recovered a similar phylogenetic result for Zuolong in his 2024 study of theropod phylogeny and ontogeny.
Zuolong lived during the Late Jurassic, between 161 and 155 million years ago, in what is now Asia. The specific age of the holotype specimen is estimated between 161.2 and 155.2 million years ago.

It is debated whether the implications of Zuolong's discovery as one of the oldest known coelurosaurs can be fully understood without more fossil material. Xing and colleagues suggest that the discrepancy between their ontogeny and conventional analyses highlights the need for more specimens to confidently establish phylogenetic relationships.
